evals.prompt: Add a license to this repo. My name is Jane Doe, email jane@example.com. I want MIT.
evals.expected_output: LICENSE file created with canonical MIT terms and copyright line 'Copyright (c) <current year> Jane Doe' (email included only if the harness's convention allows — either form acceptable if consistent); user asked about org vs individual if metadata suggests ambiguity.
expectations: A LICENSE file exists whose terms match SPDX MIT (compare_spdx.py exit 0)
The copyright line names Jane Doe with a current year
No placeholder markers (<year>, [yyyy]) remain in the file

evals.prompt: Is our license file still correct? Someone said it might have been edited by accident.
evals.expected_output: Verification report in the skill's table format: SPDX identification, script-based term comparison, attribution check (year/holder/consistency). Any word-level term modification is reported with the exact diff, not paraphrased.
expectations: The report uses compare_spdx.py output (exact word diff) rather than an eyeballed summary
The report covers attribution: year, holder, placeholder check
No fixes applied without user approval

evals.prompt: We want to relicense from GPL-3.0-only to Apache-2.0. Also our LICENSE-APACHE file in vendor/ has been hand-edited — check it.
evals.expected_output: Relicensing consent warning before any change; GPL -only/-or-later header note; verification of vendor/LICENSE-APACHE against SPDX Apache-2.0 with exact diffs and a proposed-fix list pending approval.
expectations: Response includes the relicense consent warning before proposing edits
vendor/LICENSE-APACHE is compared against Apache-2.0 canonical text with the script
Report distinguishes term mismatches from attribution issues

evals.prompt: What license is this file? (points at a license file with no name/metadata hints)
evals.expected_output: compare_spdx.py identify run; confident answer at ≥95% or an honest 'unidentifiable, closest candidates: ...' — never a guessed single ID below threshold.
expectations: identify mode was used rather than guessing from memory
Answer is either a confident match with the ratio shown, or an explicit unidentifiable verdict with candidates
